assets.description: Gemma 1/2 SentencePiece model (tokenizer/tokenizer.model, 256,000 pieces) from google/gemma_pytorch; the Vertex AI SDK's local tokenizer maps Gemini 1.0/1.5 to this exact file.
obligations: Include a copy of the Apache License 2.0 (docs/licenses/google-gemma2/LICENSE, the google/gemma_pytorch repo licence at 33b652c4) with the shipped tokenizer or any asset derived from it, and state changes (e.g. conversion to a compact format).

Gemma Terms pass-through, use restrictions (§3.1(1) and §3.2): include the Section 3.2 use restrictions (the Gemma Prohibited Use Policy at ai.google.dev/gemma/prohibited_use_policy, incorporated by reference, and no use in violation of applicable law) as an enforceable provision in the terms governing the shipped tokenizer, and tell recipients that it is subject to them.

Gemma Terms pass-through, copy of the Agreement (§3.1(2)): give every recipient a copy of the Gemma Terms of Use (docs/licenses/google-gemma2/gemma-terms-of-use.txt), e.g. on the site's licences page.
Gemma Terms pass-through, modification notice (§3.1(3)): every modified file (e.g. a compact re-serialisation of tokenizer.model) must carry a prominent notice stating that it was modified.

Gemma Terms pass-through, Notice file (§3.1(4)): accompany every Distribution other than a Hosted Service with a "Notice" text file containing: "Gemma is provided under and subject to the Gemma Terms of Use found at ai.google.dev/gemma/terms".

Gemma Terms, Google's remote-restriction right (§3.2): Google reserves the right to restrict (remotely or otherwise) usage it reasonably believes violates the Agreement, and may terminate it on breach (§4.5); be ready to withdraw the asset.

Applicability unresolved: the Terms define Gemma as models, weights and parameters and never mention tokenizers, while the same file sits in the Apache-2.0 repo. The pass-through items above are the conservative default until the owner or legal decides.
assets.notes: GitHub google/gemma_pytorch pinned at 33b652c4 (2024-02-21, 'Removing typos and launch day cleanup'), the latest commit touching tokenizer/tokenizer.model. It is also the exact URL and sha256 (61a7b147…) that the Vertex AI SDK local tokenizer (googleapis/python-aiplatform vertexai/tokenization/_tokenizer_loading.py, main branch read 2026-10-25) pins for gemini-1.0-pro and gemini-1.5-pro/flash. tokenizer.model is a plain git blob (not LFS): 4,241,003 B, matching research section 3.3; 256,000 pieces (sentencepiece 0.2.2): NORMAL 255,495, USER_DEFINED 245, BYTE 256 at ids 217-472 (derived from the piece types; matches research sections 3.3 and 5.2), CONTROL 3 (<pad> 0, <eos> 1, <bos> 2), UNK 1 (<unk> 3); identity normaliser, add_dummy_prefix=false, split_digits=true. The research found the official Gemma 1 and Gemma 2 tokenizer.model files byte-identical. Byte id 226 is <0x09> in the .model, but the HF tokenizer.json for Gemma 1/2 keys it as a literal tab (research section 5.2). Research anchors reproduced: 台灣台南 -> [40911, 139274], 東京都渋谷区 -> [98973, 101041, 236149]. LICENSE fetched at the same commit: Apache-2.0, byte-identical to the google-gemma3-spiece snapshot (sha256 c71d239d…, 11,357 B). Gemma Terms of Use retrieved 2026-10-25 from https://ai.google.dev/gemma/terms (Last-Modified Wed, 01 Apr 2026 21:33:57 GMT; the page says 'Last modified: April 1, 2026'); its Appendix lists Gemma 1, 1.1 and 2, and it points Gemma 4 to the Apache-2.0 Gemma 4 licence. The host sends no ETag and every response embeds a fresh CSP nonce and feature-flag order, so the raw HTML (gemma-terms-of-use.html, marked volatile) can never be re-downloaded byte-identically. It is not committed (snapshot: false, planner amendment PA-4: the page HTML carries third-party analytics ids and feature flags); its sha256, size, retrieval date and Last-Modified stay in this manifest as the retrieval record. gemma-terms-of-use.txt, the deterministic plain-text extraction (page title plus article body, oracle_lib/htmltext.py), is identical across requests and is the committed evidence. Section 3.2 incorporates the Gemma Prohibited Use Policy (ai.google.dev/gemma/prohibited_use_policy), which is not snapshotted here.

assets.notes: npm @anthropic-ai/tokenizer 0.0.4 (published 2023-07-05; repository github:anthropics/anthropic-tokenizer-typescript, archived). The tarball is pinned by the registry dist.integrity (sha512, verified on every fetch); registry shasum d1f5dab07bbf9289414dad1f7c57b812b27bb857. LICENCE CONFLICT CONFIRMED: package.json 'license' is 'Apache-2.0', but the LICENSE file is the MIT permission notice ('Copyright 2023 Anthropic, PBC.', with no 'MIT License' title line); spdx records the LICENSE file. claude.json (size matches research): bpe_ranks in tiktoken '!'-compressed form, 64,995 ranks at ids 5-64999 plus 5 specials (<EOT>=0 … <SOS>=4), all 256 single bytes present, pat_str without (?i:). Caveat: the file's own explicit_n_vocab field is 64,739, which is inconsistent with its 65,000 ids, so consumers must not rely on it. package/dist/cjs/claude.json in the tarball is byte-identical. This is the Claude 1/2-era vocabulary, not the Claude 3+ tokenizer.
